links.note: WAS 140 Nomenclature, which the item never touches. The two properties that give carbon its huge number of compounds are catenation and tetravalency, and the answer leads with catenation - 133.
WAS 146 Ethanoic Acid, which is only one of three structures to draw. The scored demand, and the entire model answer, is whether bromopentane has structural isomers and of what kind - 137.
WAS 146 Ethanoic Acid. The item asks WHY ethanol to ethanoic acid counts as oxidation, and the answer is the gain-of-oxygen/loss-of-hydrogen rule - organic oxidation, 142.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon, which has nothing to do with it. Butanone's group is a ketone, chosen against acid, aldehyde and alcohol - functional groups, 138.
WAS 140 Nomenclature. Why carbon compounds are used as fuels is answered entirely by their exothermic burning - combustion, 141.
WAS 149 Micelle Formation. Scum is the insoluble calcium/magnesium salt soap forms in hard water - the soap-versus-detergent property, 150; no micelle is involved.
WAS 149 Micelle Formation, which is unrelated. The item names the hydrogenatable group and explains hydrogenation with catalyst and conditions - addition reactions, 143.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism, but no isomer appears. The item asks which structures belong to the same FAMILY (alkynes) and which are not hydrocarbons - homologous series, 139.
WAS 146 Ethanoic Acid, which appears nowhere. Part (a) is the bromine-water test that ethene decolourises and methane does not - unsaturation, 136 (part (b) on ester composition would be 147).
WAS 141 Combustion. The item asks why carbon compounds are poor conductors with weak intermolecular forces, and the answer is that they are covalent - 131.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon. Buckminsterfullerene is an allotrope of carbon - 132.
WAS 144 Substitution Reactions, and the key explicitly says addition. Oils plus hydrogen over Ni/Pd is hydrogenation - addition, 143.
WAS 146 Ethanoic Acid; the answer is butanol. Identifying -OH among ketone, acid and aldehyde is a functional-group item, 138.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism; the item shows one compound, not isomers. Picking the structural formula that matches the name 'ethyne' is name-to-structure, 140.
WAS 135 Saturated Hydrocarbons. What the item tests is the condition for chlorine to react with an alkane - sunlight - which is the substitution reaction, 144.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon, a clear mis-tag. The item asks where the ionic end and the carbon chain sit in a soap micelle - 149.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism; no isomers are offered. The benzene ring is identified by its alternate single and double bonds - unsaturation, 136.
WAS 137 Structural Isomerism. Choosing the structure that matches the name 'butanoic acid' is name-to-structure, 140.
WAS 145 Ethanol, which is not even an option's answer. The IUPAC name of CH3CH2CHO is propanal - nomenclature, 140.
WAS 134 Tetravalency of Carbon. Heteroatoms (O and Br) are the atoms that carry the functional group, taught with 138.
WAS 141 Combustion; nothing is burned. Carbon bonding to four chlorines (CCl4) and to oxygen (CO2) is its tetravalency, 134.
WAS 143 Addition Reactions; no addition occurs. Compound C is ethanoic acid, identified from its reaction with sodium and with an alcohol - 146.
